TimePeriod: From Deuteronomy through Ezekiel (Late Bronze Age to exile)
Region: The Phoenician coast around Sidon, north of Tyre
History: Sidon was Canaan's firstborn (Genesis 10:15), and the Sidonians are the distinct city-people of Sidon, not Phoenicians in general: the Phoenicia entry covers Phoenicians broadly, while this entry covers Sidon itself, on the same pattern as Samaritans beside Samaria. Deuteronomy 3:9 notes that the Sidonians call Hermon Sirion. Judges 3:3 and 10:12 count Sidonians among Israel's oppressors, and Judges 18:7 describes the Zidonians as 'quiet and secure.' Solomon hired Sidonians as skilled timbermen for the temple (1 Kings 5:6), then married Sidonian wives and followed Ashtoreth, goddess of the Zidonians (1 Kings 11:1, 33). Jezebel was the daughter of Ethbaal, king of the Zidonians (1 Kings 16:31). Ezekiel 32:30 counts the Zidonians among the slain gone down to the pit. The King James Version uses both Sidonians and Zidonians for this people.
Culture: Seafarers and timbermen of the Phoenician coast, famed for cedar work and trade.
Religion: Ashtoreth, goddess of the Zidonians, carried into Israel by Solomon's Sidonian wives and by Jezebel.
BibleConnection: Sidonians touch Israel at every turn: oppressors in Judges, temple workmen under Solomon, the source of Jezebel, and the slain of Ezekiel.
KeyScriptures: Deuteronomy 3:9; Judges 3:3; Judges 10:12; Judges 18:7; 1 Kings 5:6; 1 Kings 11:1; Ezekiel 32:30
